To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a new version, the SPAI18, of the Social Pho-bia and Anxiety Inventory (Heiser et al. 2009) with good psychometric properties in both clinical and nonclinical samples, that we have validated this instrument in two different clinical samples (i.e. a sample of parents-to be) and that we have demonstrated that the SPAI- 18 is a reliable and valid instrument with good psychometric characteristics in both clinical and community samples.
the Social Phobia Scale of the SPAI was successfully reduced to 18 items (the SPAI-18) that have good internal consistency, good diagnostic characteristics, and high convergent validity.
we developed and validated a brief version of a well-validated instrument for measuring social phobia, which can be used as a diagnostic tool in both community and clinical samples.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and validation of the Social Phobic and Anxiety Inventory-18 (SPAI-18) for the assessment of social anxiety and social phobia.
the development, psychometric evaluation and validation of a short version of the SPAI.
the development and validation of a new version of a social phobia and social anxiety questionnaire, the Social Phobia Anxiety Inventory (SP AI).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SPAI- 18 is a psychometrical sound instrument with good diagnostic capacity for social anxiety disorders in clinical as well in community samples.
the SPAI- 18 is a reliable and valid instrument for the assessment of social anxiety in clinical as well in community samples.
the SPAI- 18 is a reliable and valid instrument for measuring social phobia and social anxiety disorder with a strong conceptual basis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SPAI-8 is a reliable and valid measure of social anxiety disorder and social anxiety symptoms.
the SPAI-8 and SPAI-18 are valid and reliable measures of social anxiety.
the SPAI- 18 is a reliable, valid, and easy to use instrument to measure the severity of SAD.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SPAI-8 and SPAI-18 are valid measures of social anxiety disorder and are recommended for use in research and clinical practice.
the SPAI- 18 can be used in clinical as well in community samples.
the SPAI- 18 is a psychometri- cally sound instrument for the assessment of social anxiety and social phobia.
